topic: A CASS - stages and timetable
claim: A full CASS switch takes 7 working days. The switch process begins 6 working days before the Switch Date. Working day 1: the new bank asks the old bank for outgoing payment details; days 2-3: the old bank sends them; days 4-6: they are added to the new account; day 7 (Switch Date): Direct Debits, standing orders and the remaining balance arrive, the old card is cancelled and the old account closed, and redirection starts. The customer can keep using the old account and card on days 1-6. The switch date can be chosen up to 28 days ahead (Nationwide).
quote: A full switch takes seven working days ... Working day 1 We'll ask your old provider for all your outgoing payment details. ... Working days 2-3 Your old provider will send us these details. ... Working days 4-6 We'll add these payment details to your Nationwide account. ... Working days 1-6 You can keep using your old account and card during your switch. ... Working day 7 Your switch is complete! Your Direct Debits, standing orders and any money left in your old bank account have now been moved ... Your old provider will cancel your card and close your old account. ... 1.4 The switch process begins 6 working days before the Switch Date. We will tell you that the switch is underway and when it is completed, and also if there is any reason why your switch request cannot be initiated or completed.
source: Nationwide Building Society, Current Account Switch Service guide incl. the CASS Guarantee, Current Account Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction (P2205, May 2026)
appliesTo: UK (all players with UK current accounts)
uncertainty: Low. The day-by-day split is Nationwide's wording; Co-operative Bank and Santander describe the same 7 days in slightly different groupings (Co-op: days 1-2 checks, 3-5 payments, 6-7 balance and closure). The 28-day-ahead window is Nationwide's, not verified as a CASS-wide rule.
suggestedSimplification: Model a switch as: apply (day 0) -> switch date chosen >= 7 working days ahead -> day 7 balance moves, payments move, old account closes, redirection begins.

topic: A CASS - balance transfer and held funds
claim: The credit balance moves on the Switch Date. The old bank keeps enough to cover transactions still clearing and debit-card authorisations not yet paid, then forwards the rest, credited to the new account no later than the next working day after it is released.
quote: 1.11 Funds will be retained by your Old Bank to cover any transactions made before the Switch Date on your Old Account which are still in the process of being cleared on the Switch Date. On the day that your Old Bank no longer needs to retain funds to cover transactions that are being cleared, it will transfer them to your New Account and they will be credited to your New Account no later than the next working day.
source: Nationwide Building Society, Current Account Switch Service guide incl. the CASS Guarantee, Current Account Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction (P2205, May 2026)
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Move the whole balance on the switch date; ignore held-back clearing funds.

topic: A CASS - new bank declines / switch cannot start
claim: No CASS page found that describes a declined application verbatim. CASS runs only after the new account is opened and the customer signs the Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction, so a declined account application means no switch starts and the old account is untouched (inference). The Guarantee promises contact before the switch date if there are issues.
quote: If there are any issues in making the switch, we will contact you before your switch date. ... 1.4 ... We will tell you ... if there is any reason why your switch request cannot be initiated or completed.
source: Nationwide Building Society, Current Account Switch Service guide incl. the CASS Guarantee, Current Account Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction (P2205, May 2026)
uncertainty: The "declined -> nothing happens" outcome is an inference from the sequence (open account, then consent), not a quoted rule. Not found: an official statement on what happens if the new bank declines.
suggestedSimplification: If the new bank refuses the account, no switch is created; the old account stays as it was.

topic: A CASS - overdraft or debt on the old account
claim: An overdrawn customer can still switch. The overdraft is not carried over; the customer agrees a new overdraft with the new bank (which may pay off a set amount of the old overdraft on day 7, Nationwide) or repays it separately. If debt remains after the Switch Date, the switch still completes: the old account is blocked for everything except repayment, its terms continue, it closes when the debt is repaid, and the old bank may use redirected incoming funds to settle the debt.
quote: 3. Unless I have outstanding debt on my Old Account, closure of my Old Account will be effective from my Switch Date. I understand that, whether or not I have an outstanding debt on my Old Account, my Old Account will not be available for use from my Switch Date ... 11. If I have outstanding debt on my Old Account (including any fees or charges) after my Switch Date, my Old Bank will tell me. In such circumstances: my Old Bank will block my Old Account and I will not be able to carry out any further transactions on it, with the exception of repaying the outstanding debt; and the terms and conditions of my Old Account will continue to apply until I have repaid the outstanding debt in full, at which time my Old Account will be closed. 12. If there is an outstanding debt on my Old Account after my Switch Date, my Old Bank will be entitled to use any funds or payments it receives (including by cheque) in full, or part, settlement of the debt on my Old Account.
source: Nationwide Building Society, Current Account Switch Service guide incl. the CASS Guarantee, Current Account Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction (P2205, May 2026) (Account Closure Instruction, standard CASS wording)
uncertainty: Low; this is the CASS Account Closure Instruction as reproduced by one participant. It supersedes the "switch fails before the switch date" simplification in research-tax-switch-lending.json (B6 timing and overdraft), which was a guess. The CASS FAQ also says, paraphrased in fetch, that without agreement with the new bank the customer must arrange repayment of the old overdraft separately.
suggestedSimplification: The switch always proceeds. Leftover old-account debt stays as a blocked account, closed when repaid, that keeps its own interest/fees and absorbs any redirected incoming money.

topic: A CASS - cancelling a switch
claim: The switch date can be changed, and the switch cancelled outright, until close of business 7 working days before the Switch Date. There is also a 14-calendar-day right to cancel the Switch Agreement, but once the 6-working-day process has begun the Account Closure Instruction cannot be cancelled: the old account still closes and payment mandates still move; only the balance transfer can be stopped, if notice reaches the old bank before close of business on the working day before the Switch Date. A completed step is never reversed.
quote: You can cancel your switch up to seven working days before your switch date. [CASS FAQ] ... 1.3 You can change the Switch Date at any time up until the close of business 7 working days before the Switch Date ... If you cancel this Agreement, any account switch processes already completed cannot be reversed or unwound. ... 2. During the 6 working days before the Switch Date: Your Old Account will be closed from the Switch Date because your Account Closure Instruction cannot be cancelled. ... The transfer of your Old Account balance to your New Account will be stopped provided we have enough time to notify your Old Bank that you have cancelled the Agreement before your Old Bank closes for business on the working day before the Switch.
source: CASS Common questions; Nationwide Building Society, Current Account Switch Service guide incl. the CASS Guarantee, Current Account Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction (P2205, May 2026)
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Cancel freely until 7 working days before the switch date; after that the old account closes regardless.

topic: A CASS - switch failure partway (the Guarantee)
claim: If anything goes wrong (a payment not redirected, redirected wrongly, or lost), the new bank corrects the error and refunds interest and charges incurred, paid or lost on either account because of the failure, once told.
quote: If anything goes wrong with the switch, as soon as we are told, we will refund any interest (paid or lost) and charges made on either your old or new current accounts as a result of this failure. ... 2.2 If something goes wrong with the Current Account Switch Service (for example if a payment is not redirected, is redirected incorrectly, or is lost), we will correct the error, you will receive a refund of any interest and/or charges incurred, paid or lost on your Old Account or your New Account as a result of the failure and we will notify you of any action we have taken and the outcome.
source: Nationwide Building Society, Current Account Switch Service guide incl. the CASS Guarantee, Current Account Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction (P2205, May 2026) (Guarantee and Agreement 2.2)
uncertainty: Not found: a CASS rule for a switch that halts midway (e.g. old bank fails to send mandates); the Guarantee covers consequences, not a rollback. The Guarantee does not apply to a partial switch.
suggestedSimplification: On a switch error, refund any fee or interest it caused; the switch still completes.

topic: A CASS - debit card recurring payments
claim: Recurring card payments (continuous payment authorities, card-on-file subscriptions) are not moved and not redirected; the customer must give each merchant the new card details. Direct Debits and standing orders do move.
quote: A full switch will not: Automatically update your card information for any subscription payments linked to your Debit Card (using the long card number), such as Netflix or Amazon Prime. Update your card details in any mobile payment services or digital wallets. Automatically apply any overdraft you have with your old provider. [Nationwide] ... payment requests sent to your old account will not be redirected. [Co-operative Bank]
source: Nationwide Building Society, Current Account Switch Service guide incl. the CASS Guarantee, Current Account Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction (P2205, May 2026); Co-operative Bank FAQ PROD-2473
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Card subscriptions fail after the switch date until the player re-enters the new card.

topic: A CASS - payment redirection period
claim: Redirection runs for 3 years after the Switch Date and auto-extends until there is a 13-month period with no redirected Direct Debit, Bacs credit or Faster Payment. Each redirected payment tells the sender the new details. The customer can end redirection at any time.
quote: 1.13 For 3 years after the Switch Date if your Old Bank receives payments or requests for payments which relate to your Old Account, subject to compliance with applicable laws, it will redirect these to your New Account. ... 1.14 In the unlikely event that payments continue to be redirected to your New Account during the 13 months leading up to the end of the 3 year redirection period we will automatically extend the redirection service and the term of this Agreement until such time as there is a 13 month period when no Direct Debits, Bacs Direct Credits or Faster Payment transactions have been automatically redirected ...
source: Nationwide Building Society, Current Account Switch Service guide incl. the CASS Guarantee, Current Account Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction (P2205, May 2026) (Agreement 1.13-1.14)
uncertainty: Low. Reconciles the NatWest "indefinite" statement in research-tax-switch-lending.json: indefinite in practice while payments keep arriving.
suggestedSimplification: Redirect for 36 months, extended while any redirected payment arrived in the last 13 months.

topic: A CASS - partial switch
claim: A partial switch moves payments but leaves the old account open, takes up to 20 working days, and is not covered by the Guarantee, Switch Agreement or Account Closure Instruction.
quote: Take up to 20 working days to complete. ... The following do not apply to a partial switch: - Current Account Switch Guarantee - Current Account Switch Agreement - Current Account Closure Instruction
source: Nationwide Building Society, Current Account Switch Service guide incl. the CASS Guarantee, Current Account Switch Agreement and Account Closure Instruction (P2205, May 2026)
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Optional; omit partial switches.

topic: B US - no switching service; steps
claim: No US equivalent of CASS was found. Moving accounts is manual: open the new account, redirect direct deposit by giving the employer the new routing/account numbers, move each automatic payment individually, keep both accounts open until deposits land at the new bank, then close the old one. No branded "switch kit" was found at Chase, Bank of America, Citi or Capital One (smaller banks and AAA publish them).
quote: Keep both accounts open until the direct deposit starts hitting the new account (search summary of Capital One Learn & Grow and third-party guides)
source: Capital One, How to Switch Banks and Move Your Checking Account (Learn & Grow); search results
uncertainty: The quote is a search-result summary, not a fetched verbatim quote. Big-bank switch kits: not found (search only, not exhaustive).
suggestedSimplification: US switching is a player to-do list: each payee and employer updated separately; nothing redirects; the old account stays open until the player closes it.

Amounts $2,500-$40,000; terms 36, 48, 60, 72 or 84 months; no fees of any kind. Eligibility: valid US SSN, age 18+, individual or household income at least $25,000, physical address, email. Individual borrowers only (no co-borrowers). Cannot be used to pay any Capital One/Discover account, or a post-secondary education loan or expense.
quote: Have a valid U.S. SSN ... Be at least 18 years old ... Have a minimum individual or household annual income of at least $25,000 ... Because Discover personal loans are only for individual borrowers, co-borrowing is not permitted. ... A Discover personal loan is intended for personal use and cannot be used to directly pay any Capital One account (including any Discover or Capital One credit card), secured loan, or post-secondary education loan or expense. ... No Fees. Period. ... a division of Capital One, N.A., Member FDIC

No citizenship/permanent-resident rule found on Discover pages.

topic: D IRS - Simple Payment Plan (formerly streamlined)
claim: As of July 2026 the IRS calls the long-term plan for balances of $50,000 or less a "Simple Payment Plan". No Collection Information Statement is needed. The earlier 72-month payment rule was removed: the balance must be paid in full by the Collection Statute Expiration Date (generally 10 years from assessment).
quote: 5.14.5.2(1) A Simple Payment Plan may be granted when all of the following criteria are met: (1) The aggregate unpaid balance of assessment (the CC SUMRY balance) is $50,000 or less ... (7) A Collection Information Statement (CIS) is not required when the account meets the criteria for a Simple Payment Plan. [Topic 202:] must pay the tax liability in full by the Collection Statute Expiration Date
source: IRM 5.14.5 (07-21-2026); IRS Tax Topic 202 (updated 25-Sep-2026)
appliesTo: US citizen and F-1 (1040 or 1040-NR filers)
uncertainty: The "72-month rule removed" statement came from the fetch summary of the IRM material-changes note, not a verbatim quote. Minimum payment: no fixed formula found; computed so the balance pays off by the CSED.
suggestedSimplification: Plan runs until paid, at most 10 years; monthly payment at least balance / months left to the CSED.

topic: D IRS - guaranteed installment agreement
claim: Guaranteed if: tax owed $10,000 or less excluding interest and penalties; timely filed and paid for the past 5 years; no IA in the past 5 years; pay in full within 3 years; unable to pay in full when due.
quote: You agree to pay the full amount you owe within 3 years ... During the past 5 tax years, you (and your spouse if filing a joint return) have timely filed all income tax returns
source: Instructions for Form 9465 (Rev. 07/2024); Topic 202
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Optional tier: <= $10k always accepted.

topic: D IRS - setup and revision fees
claim: Short-term (<= 180 days, < $100,000): $0. Long-term: $29 online direct debit; $107 direct debit by phone/mail/in person; $69 online non-direct-debit; $178 non-direct-debit by phone/mail/in person; low-income: $0 direct debit, $43 otherwise (may be reimbursed). Revising an existing plan: $6 online, $89 by phone/mail/in person, $0 for direct-debit changes. Reinstatement after default: $6 online (OPA), $89 by regulation ($43 low income).
quote: Revising an existing plan: $6 online; $89 by phone/mail/in-person [fetch summary of payment-plans page] ... The fee for restructuring or reinstating an installment agreement on or after January 1, 2017, is $89. ... then the fee ... is $43. [26 CFR 300.2(b)]
source: IRS Payment plans page (13-Aug-2026); IRS OPA page (14-Sep-2026); 26 CFR 300.2
uncertainty: 26 CFR 300.1 on Cornell shows older entry fees ($225/$107/$149/$31); the IRS.gov amounts are current. Revision fee figures are fetch summaries.
suggestedSimplification: Charge $29 to set up online with direct debit, $6 to revise or reinstate online.

topic: D IRS - penalty and interest during a plan
claim: Interest continues. The failure-to-pay penalty is halved to 0.25% a month for any month an installment agreement under IRC 6159 is in effect, but only for an individual who filed on time (including extensions).
quote: In the case of an individual who files a return of tax on or before the due date for the return (including extensions), paragraphs (2) and (3) of subsection (a) shall each be applied by substituting "0.25" for "0.5" each place it appears for purposes of determining the addition to tax for any month during which an installment agreement under section 6159 is in effect for the payment of such tax.
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: 0.25%/month on a plan if filed on time; else 0.5%.

topic: D IRS - missed payment / default
claim: Default occurs on a missed payment or on failing to pay a later tax liability when due. The taxpayer receives CP523 (Installment Agreement Default Notice - Notice of Intent to Levy) and has 30 days to comply before termination; the collection statute is suspended 30 days. A reinstatement fee may apply.
quote: 5.14.11.4(2) A taxpayer with an IDRS monitored installment agreement will receive Notice CP 523, Installment Agreement Default Notice - Notice of Intent to Levy. ... (1) ... notified in writing and given 30 days to comply with the terms of the agreement before the agreement is terminated. [i9465:] If you don't make your payments on time or don't timely pay a balance due on a return you file later, you will be in default on your agreement and we may terminate the agreement. [payment plans page:] There may be a reinstatement fee if your plan goes into default.
source: IRM 5.14.11; Form 9465 instructions; IRS Payment plans page
uncertainty: IRM 5.14.11 section date not captured.
suggestedSimplification: Missed payment -> CP523 -> 30 days to catch up (with $6/$89 reinstatement) -> else plan terminated and levy possible.

topic: D IRS - adding a later assessment (e.g. amended return)
claim: A new balance not paid when due puts the plan in default. It can be folded in by revising/reinstating the agreement; IRS staff may reinstate without manager approval if adding the new liability adds no more than two monthly payments.
quote: 5.14.11.5(2)(a) The agreement is in default or was terminated because of an additional liability and if addition of that new liability will result in no more than two additional monthly payments.
uncertainty: No IRS.gov consumer page found saying explicitly that a new balance can be added online; the OPA page lists changing amount/date and reinstating. Whether the OPA tool accepts an added balance: not found.
suggestedSimplification: A later assessment triggers a revise (fee $6 online) that adds it to the plan, raising the monthly payment.

topic: D IRS - refund offset during a plan
claim: Refunds are applied to the balance while a plan is in effect, and the monthly payment is still due.
quote: Any refund will be applied against the amount you owe even if you have an installment agreement. If your refund is applied to your balance, you're still required to make your regular monthly installment payment. [i9465] ... Your future refunds will be applied to your tax debt until it is paid in full. [payment plans page]
source: Form 9465 instructions; IRS Payment plans page
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: Refund reduces plan balance; monthly payment unchanged.

topic: D IRS - all returns filed; how to apply
claim: All required returns must be filed before a plan is granted. Apply online (OPA, needs an IRS Online Account with photo ID) or by Form 9465; a mailed 9465 is typically answered within 30 days.
quote: 5.14.1.4.2(5) Do not grant agreements if the taxpayers have not filed all required returns. ... If you mail Form 9465, the IRS will respond to your request typically within 30 days
uncertainty: Low.
suggestedSimplification: An unfiled return blocks any plan.

topic: D IRS - nonresident aliens (1040-NR)
claim: No rule found barring nonresident aliens from installment agreements; IRS international-taxpayer pages point taxpayers abroad to the OPA, and Form 9465 instructions give a filing address for foreign addresses (Austin). Caveat: the OPA needs an IRS Online Account with identity verification, which may be harder without an SSN; Form 9465 asks for SSN/EIN (ITIN holders presumably use ITIN).
quote: Department of the Treasury Internal Revenue Service 3651 South I-H 35 5501AUSC Austin, TX 78741 [i9465 address for foreign addresses]
source: Form 9465 instructions; IRS international taxpayer pages (search)
uncertainty: Not found: any explicit IRS statement on 1040-NR filers and installment agreements, or on ITIN use with the OPA. IRM 5.14.1 and 5.14.4 contain no nonresident-specific guidance.
suggestedSimplification: Treat 1040-NR filers like anyone else for plans; an F-1 without an SSN applies by Form 9465 (mail, about 30 days) rather than online.
